_comment: Sound design for the revised chapter 6. Built from assets that already
exist, so it cost no ElevenLabs credits.
THE QUIET EVENT STILL GOVERNS: local machinery and the world outside, never
a settlement alarm. Nobody sounds a siren in these chapters.
Levels are DERIVED from audio/config.json's categoryTargetLufs and each
asset's measured loudness. `emphasisDb` is the only hand-set number, and in
this movement it is mostly one sound: the deep distant vibration, which
gets louder every time it returns.

cues.why: Back in the laboratory for the whole chapter. The bed returns as the vehicle arrives, which closes the round trip Chapter 5 opened.
The environmental sensor reading out into the console.
The wrist-camera recording arriving on the main screen, with the fingernail clipping on it.
Advancing the footage a frame at a time. Three dB under the chapter's other typing: this is one finger, not two hands working.
Jack searching the original TOMBS calibration records for the scale target.
The surviving parameter block coming up: 'Target height normalization', the line that proves somebody chose how small.
The maintenance partition opening, filling the screen with machine data the intruder did not erase.

A single flat system tone as the creation time is checked against the island clock and the backup server. Not an alarm -- four dB down, and the same tone Chapter 1 uses when TOMBS refuses him -- because what it marks is a machine calmly confirming something nobody wants confirmed.
'Three words appeared on the screen.' The notify tone lands just before the narration, so the listener hears the screen answer and is then told what it said: PHASE ONE READY.

'Outside, something struck the distant ground.' The last sound of the movement and the loudest, +8 dB -- one step beyond the boundary vibration in Chapter 5, because the point of the ending is that it is still coming.

'The control-room window trembled.' The building's answer to it, under the line. Nothing sounds after this: the chapter ends on 'It had gone exactly the way someone planned', and that belongs to the narrator alone.
